sections.feedback log: - 2026-10-12, user chat (no panel, no capture file): "both of i06 survived, others not tested". Form quick test of sketch i06 in its lean and explicit wordings (notes/sketches/i06.md), answer as in this file. A quick test is a first screen against the easier solver; it sets no tier. sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: a membership filter across two tables that describe the same measures (ratings in one, listed costs and benefits in the other), with one member carried over by a cross-reference; medium. Measured: the sketch's two wordings both survived the form's quick test (user, 2026-10-12, chat only); no difficulty run yet.
- Dependency plan: D02 L391-436 (ratings in the order costs, benefits, implementation challenges; header L392-394) -> seven measures rated High then Low (L418, L424, L427, L429, L431, L434, L435). D04 L828-912 (Annex 2) -> independence listed for row 11 (L884) and row 5 (L859), carried into row 3 by "All other benefits of 1 above" (L845, row 1's benefit at L833); none for rows 2, 9, 14, 15. Intersection: tendering and rotation reform, audit-only split, joint audits.
- Universe: Deloitte's seventeen rated measures. High for costs and Low for benefits: (1) reform mandatory tendering and auditor rotation, in; (2) prohibit non-audit services to all large clients and PIEs, out (D04 row 2, L835-840: audit quality and competition only); (3) split into audit-only and non-audit practices, in by cross-reference; (4) joint audits, in; (5) break-up into smaller firms, out (D04 row 9, L877 "Immediate impact on market concentration"); (6) insurance-based system, out (D04 row 14, costs only); (7) NAO-style national auditor, out (D04 row 15: "Consistency of approach and standards", "Accountability and 'public interest' credentials"). The other ten fail the rating: audit-client ban Medium High, market share cap High High, stronger governance Medium High, shared audits and peer review Medium Medium, direct support Medium Medium, staff switching Low Medium, ownership Medium Low, tendering transparency Low Medium, audit committees Low Medium, break the link Low Low.
- Necessity: D02 is the only document that rates measures (rating triples occur only at D02 L398-435); without it no measure is High/Low. D04's Annex 2 is the only per-measure list of benefits; without it nothing separates three of the seven. Substitutes searched: ICAEW's comments on each measure (D06 L172-228) credit "the perceived independence of auditors" to the non-audit-service restrictions as a group and to more frequent tendering, a different set that the question excludes by naming Grant Thornton; no other document lists benefits by measure. No removal probes run (optional diagnostics, none requested).
- Bundle independence: the CMA's measures are public, but the answer needs Deloitte's seven ratings and Grant Thornton's row entries; a guess would have to name exactly these three of about seventeen. The question prints no number.
- Selected-lever checks (which-items): decoys named in the reasoning. Break the link: independence benefit in D04 (L896), fails D02's rating (L433 "4.40 Low Low High"). All-clients prohibition: passes D02's rating (L424), no independence benefit in D04. Without the exclusion the answer is the seven measures of the Universe line.
- Targeted failure modes: (1) Document convention: rows read one at a time, "All other benefits of 1 above" (D04 L845) not followed: tendering and rotation reform and joint audits only. (2) Linking across documents: D04 row 1 (restrictions on non-audit services "to their audit clients", L830, "Promotes auditor independence") matched to D02's "Prohibit audit firms from providing non-audit services to all large clients and PIEs" (L423-424): a fourth measure. Considered and not declared: Deloitte's "Measures that we do not support" heading taken for the rating (split, joint audits and break the link); "joint and shared audits" given as one item. No solver trace has been seen: align the modes with the difficulty run's observed wrong answers before Submit.
- Calculation verification: not applicable (no arithmetic). Both tables re-read line by line by the caller on 2026-10-12 after two independent authors' reads; every evidence quote found once in docs/ (character offsets checked by script).
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: the bundle overview mentions neither table. Searches: rating triples (D02 only), "independence" in D04 Annex 2 (L833, L859, L884, L886, L896, L897), "All other benefits" (D04 L845 only). Shortest complete route is the six steps above.
- Precision/readings: column order fixed by the header (L392-394) and confirmed in prose (D02 L443 "The challenges on implementation would be less significant" for the row rated Medium High Low; L471 "The costs associated with tendering are already high" for the row rated High Low Medium). Tendering's benefit is hedged ("Potentially") but listed as a benefit; the question asks what the list gives. Grant Thornton's main text on the split points both ways (D04 L28, L295), so the question names the costs-and-benefits list and says a carried-over benefit counts. Joint audits: D04 row 5 covers joint and shared audits together; D02 rates the two separately and only joint audits is High then Low; D04 L349 also says "Joint audits offer more technical knowledge, quality, independence".
- Completeness: no known source gaps (10 of 10 documents read in full; hashes match the capture).
- Style/set review: plain wording, organisations named, no file or page references; 46 words. The explicit wording was chosen over the lean one because both survived the quick test (most explicit survivor). "if any" and "List them in any order." were added after the quick test for the form's answer-format check, and the answer's second item was shortened from "splitting UK firms into audit-only and non-audit practices" so that commas alone separate the items; none of this changes a condition or a member. q01 (dropped) shares no input. Sketch i08 shares the tendering row and stays unused.
- Warnings answered: origin claude (the form's authorship tick is the user's). list-items: the floor cannot place item boundaries because the first item's own name contains "and" ("tendering and auditor rotation"); the three items are comma-separated and equal the three components.

sections.question: Which of the CMA's potential measures, if any, does Deloitte rate High for costs and Low for benefits, although greater auditor independence is among the benefits Grant Thornton's costs-and-benefits list gives them, whether stated outright or carried over from another measure? List them in any order.
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 2, summary table of measures in the appendix): Deloitte gives each measure a rating for costs, then benefits, then implementation challenges. The measures rated High for costs and Low for benefits are: reform of mandatory tendering and auditor rotation, prohibiting non-audit services to all large clients and PIEs, splitting UK firms into audit-only and non-audit practices, joint audits, break-up of the largest firms into smaller audit firms, an insurance-based system, and an NAO-style national auditor.
Step 2. Check (Doc 2, same table): the table's group headings are not the test. Tendering and rotation reform sits under "Other measures that appear to have merit" and is still rated High, then Low. "Break link between company management and auditors" sits under "Measures that we do not support" but is rated Low for costs, so it is not a candidate.
Step 3. Source input (Doc 4, annex of costs and benefits, one numbered row per measure): the row for reforming mandatory tendering and auditor rotation lists "Potentially strengthen auditor independence" as a benefit, and the row for joint and shared audits lists "Effective at promoting independence".
Step 4. Source input (Doc 4, same annex): the row for splitting the firms into audit-only and non-audit practices closes its benefits with "All other benefits of 1 above". Row 1 is the restriction on non-audit services to audit clients, and its benefits begin "Promotes auditor independence", so the split carries that benefit over.
Step 5. Source input (Doc 4, same annex): the rows for prohibiting non-audit services to any other large company or PIE, breaking up the largest firms, the insurance-based system and the NAO-style auditor list no independence benefit and point to no other row's benefits.
Step 6. Filter (Doc 2 and Doc 4): of the measures in Step 1, those given an independence benefit in Doc 4 are tendering and rotation reform, the audit-only split and joint audits. Doc 2 rates shared audits Medium for costs, so only joint audits comes out of Doc 4's joint-and-shared row.
Decoys: breaking the link between management and auditors, which Doc 4 calls the "Strongest solution to concerns over audit independence" but Doc 2 rates Low for costs; and the prohibition for all large clients, rated High then Low in Doc 2 but given no independence benefit in Doc 4.
Final answer (Doc 2 and Doc 4): Reform of mandatory tendering and auditor rotation, the audit-only split of UK firms, joint audits.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Document convention
How a careless solver fails: Wrong members in a list

### Failure mode 2
Trap: Linking across documents
How a careless solver fails: Picks the wrong entity or section

Why these are traps: Document convention: Doc 4's annex gives the audit-only split its independence benefit only as "All other benefits of 1 above"; read row by row, two measures remain. Linking across documents: matching Doc 4's audit-client restriction to Doc 2's all-clients prohibition adds a fourth. The gold follows the cross-reference.
